strings.title: Give and Take
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: When one number is close to a hundred or a thousand, give it what it needs from the other number. The total stays the same: 298 + 145 = 300 + 143.
strings.keywords: give and take, friendly number, close to, total stays the same, compensate
watchFor: Making the friendly number but forgetting to take from the other (298 + 145 = 445): ask "Where did the 2 come from?"
Taking from the wrong number, or giving too much: ask "How much does 298 need to make 300?"
Lining up the algorithm when the numbers are friendly: ask "Is one number close to a hundred?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why does the total stay the same?" Land: moving an amount from one number to the other doesn't change the total. Make one number friendly, then the adding is easy.

problems.notes: Look for: a quick friendly sum. Ask: "Hold on to this one." Model: split 300 + 145
Look for: 298 gets 2 from 145: 300 + 143. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Word choice: "give and take". Model: givetake 298 + 145 = 300 + 143

responses.tip: Gave 2 but didn't take it. Ask: where did the 2 come from?

problems.notes: Look for: 500 + 237. Ask: "What does 499 need?" Model: givetake 499 + 238 = 500 + 237
Look for: 2000 + 345. Ask: "Is it the same idea with thousands?" Model: givetake 1998 + 347 = 2000 + 345
Look for: 4000 + 2001. Ask: "Which number should give?" Model: givetake 3995 + 2006 = 4000 + 2001

responses.tip: Either number can give. Ask: which was easier?
Added the 5 back instead of taking it away. Ask: is 3995 more or less than 4000?

problems.notes: Look for: 1500 + 2500. Ask: "What do you notice about these numbers?" Model: givetake 1499 + 2501 = 1500 + 2500

responses.tip: A neat one: both become friendly.

strings.title: Adding Four-Digit Numbers
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Add big numbers by place value (thousands, hundreds, tens, ones), or by making one number friendly first.
strings.keywords: thousands, hundreds, place value, split, give and take, friendly number
watchFor: Lining up digits from the left when the numbers have different lengths: ask "Which digit is the thousands?"
Forgetting to regroup ten hundreds as a thousand: ask "What do 6 hundreds and 4 hundreds make?"
Not noticing 3998 is close to 4000: ask "Is either number close to a friendly number?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "When did you split by place value, and when did you make a number friendly?" Land: split when the numbers are ordinary; make one friendly when it's close to a thousand or hundred.

problems.notes: Look for: 2 thousands and 1 thousand. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: split 2000 + 1000
Look for: 3000 + 700. Ask: "What are the parts?" Model: split 2400 + 1300
Look for: 3000 + 700 + 120 + 5. Ask: "What happens in the tens?" Model: split 2450 + 1375

responses.tip: Ask: what do 5 tens and 7 tens make?
Lost the hundred from the tens. Ask: what is 50 + 70?

problems.notes: Look for: 3998 needs 2 to make 4000. Ask: "Is either number close to a friendly number?" Model: givetake 3998 + 1250 = 4000 + 1248

responses.tip: Gave 2 but didn't take it. Ask: where did the 2 come from?

problems.notes: Look for: 625 + 375 = 1000. Ask: "What do you notice about 625 and 375?" Model: split 4625 + 2375
Look for: 1875 + 125 = 2000, then 2225 more. Ask: "What does 1875 need to make 2000?" Model: numberline 1875 +125 +2225
Look for: 7000 + 2500 − 2. Ask: "Could you make both friendly?" Model: text 6999 + 2499 = 7000 + 2500 - 2 = 9498

strings.title: Adding and Subtracting: Choose a Strategy
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Look at the numbers first, then choose: split by place value, make a friendly number, count up, or take away. Each subtraction here undoes the addition before it.
strings.keywords: choose, inverse, undo, add up, take away, give and take, friendly number
watchFor: Using one strategy for everything: ask "What do you notice about these numbers?"
Not seeing the related addition: ask "Did the problem before help?"
Not checking: ask "How could you check with adding?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did each addition help with the subtraction after it?" Land: addition and subtraction undo each other. If 48 + 37 = 85, then 85 − 37 = 48. Check every subtraction by adding.

problems.notes: Look for: 48 + 2 = 50, + 35. Or 70 + 15. Ask: "Which way did you go?" Model: numberline 48 +2 +35
Look for: it undoes the last one. Ask: "Do you even need to work it out?" Word choice: "undo". Model: numberline 37 >40 >85

responses.tip: Addition and subtraction undo each other.

problems.notes: Look for: 300 + 455. Ask: "What's 299 close to?" Model: givetake 299 + 456 = 300 + 455
Look for: the last one undone, or 755 − 300 + 1. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Model: numberline 755 -300 +1

responses.tip: Ask: did 300 take away too much or too little?

problems.notes: Look for: back 3 to 600, back 4. Ask: "Take away or add up?" Model: numberline 603 -3 -4
Look for: 589 up 11 to 600, up 3. Ask: "Why count up this time?" Model: numberline 589 >600 >603

responses.tip: Algorithm slip. Ask: are 603 and 589 close?

problems.notes: Look for: 250 + 750 = 1000. Ask: "What do 250 and 750 make?" Model: split 1250 + 1750
